subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: The radius of a circle is increasing at the rate of 0.7 cm/sec. What is the rate of increase of its circumference?

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you would write, and say why the question gives you no radius.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate C = 2πr with respect to t
steps.margin_note: First mark. C = 2πr is linear in r, so differentiating leaves the constant 2π and no r at all. That is why the question gives no radius.
lines: Circumference of a circle of radius r:  C = 2πr
Differentiate both sides with respect to time t:

recall.must_convey: That C = 2πr differentiated with respect to t gives dC/dt = 2π(dr/dt), with no r left in it.
accept: circumference is two pi r so d c by d t is two pi d r by d t
differentiate the circumference formula with respect to time
two pi is a constant so no radius is left
circumference formula ni time tho differentiate cheyyali
d c by d t equals two pi into d r by d t
the radius disappears because the formula is linear in r

steps.why: The circumference is a constant multiple of the radius, so its time rate is the same constant multiple of dr/dt. No instant has to be named, which is why no radius is given.
common_mistakes: Using the area formula πr², which brings in a radius the question does not give.
Differentiating 2πr as 2π r² or as πr.
Deciding the question is incomplete because no radius is stated.
steps.memory_tip: C = 2πr is a straight-line relation between C and r, so their rates keep the same fixed ratio 2π at every size.

steps.label: Substitute dr/dt = 0.7
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 2π × 0.7 = 1.4π. State plainly that the answer holds for a circle of any radius — that observation is what the question is testing.
lines: This value contains no r, so the circumference increases at this same rate whatever the radius is.

recall.must_convey: That dC/dt = 2π(0.7) = 1.4π cm/sec, and that the answer does not depend on the radius.
accept: two pi into zero point seven is one point four pi
the answer is one point four pi centimetres per second
it does not depend on the radius at all
radius meeda depend avvadu, answer one point four pi
the circumference grows at a constant rate for a constant d r by d t
about four point four centimetres per second
heard_as: does not depend on the radius

steps.why: A circumference is a length, so its rate is a length per second, cm/sec. Saying that the rate is the same at every radius shows the relation was understood and not just substituted into.
common_mistakes: Multiplying 2 × 0.7 and writing 1.4 without the π.
Giving the unit as cm²/sec, which belongs to an area rate.
Adding a radius value that the question never supplied.
steps.memory_tip: Doubling 0.7 gives 1.4, so the answer is simply 1.4π — the π stays because 2π was the constant in the formula.
